findings.body: `find_by` returns nil and `nil.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 error page instead of unsubscribing the user.
findings.evidence:
tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])

    if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
findings.failure_mode: Unhandled NoMethodError at runtime on a user-facing GET endpoint linked from every notification email.
findings.impact: `find_by` returns nil and `nil.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 error page instead of unsubscribing the user.
findings.root_cause: The new action assumes a TopicUser record always exists for the current user and topic and dereferences the `find_by` result without a nil check.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the nil case, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` then `return redirect_to @topic_view.topic.relative_url` / create the record via `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` instead of mutating a possibly nil record.
findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.trigger: A logged-in user opens /t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe for a topic that has no topic_users row for them (never opened the topic, row pruned, or notification delivered without creating the row).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R105-R107 show `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` followed immediately by `tu.notification_level` with no nil guard. `find_by` returns nil when no record exists, causing NoMethodError on nil.notification_level. Trigger is realistic: user clicks unsubscribe link for topic they never opened.

raw_findings.body: The victim's notification level for the targeted topic is silently downgraded or muted without any interaction on their part.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unauthenticated cross-site or automated requests mutate per-user notification state.
raw_findings.impact: The victim's notification level for the targeted topic is silently downgraded or muted without any interaction on their part.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch wires a mutating controller action (`tu.save!`) to a plain GET route, which is not CSRF-protected and is safely prefetchable by intermediaries.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the GET route render a confirmation page only and perform the mutation from a POST/PUT endpoint (or require a signed one-time unsubscribe key in the URL) before calling `tu.save!`.
raw_findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET without confirmation

raw_findings.body: The layout is rendered eagerly by the explicit `render`, so `@canonical_url` set afterwards is ignored and the `<link rel="canonical">` tag disappears from topic pages, an SEO regression.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silently missing canonical metadata in the rendered HTML for all topic pages.
raw_findings.impact: The layout is rendered eagerly by the explicit `render`, so `@canonical_url` set afterwards is ignored and the `<link rel="canonical">` tag disappears from topic pages, an SEO regression.
raw_findings.root_cause: Adding an explicit `render :show` inside `perform_show_response` moves template/layout rendering earlier than the `canonical_url` assignment that used to run before the implicit render.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the implicit render for `show` (e.g. render explicitly only from `unsubscribe`, or move the `canonical_url` call before `perform_show_response`).
raw_findings.title: Explicit `render :show` makes canonical_url in #show a no-op
raw_findings.trigger: Any crawler or non-XHR HTML request to a topic page (`topics#show`), which calls `perform_show_response` and only afterwards executes `canonical_url UrlHelper.absolute_without_cdn(...)`.

raw_findings.body: The notification reason paragraph rendered by `topic-notifications-button` (longDescription alias) is not suppressed, or reappears after the first level change, contradicting the stated intent of the code.

raw_findings.root_cause: The route mutates a computed property that has no setter, so the assignment is either clobbered or recomputed by its dependent keys.

validated_findings.impact: The layout is rendered eagerly by the explicit `render`, so `@canonical_url` set afterwards is ignored and the `<link rel="canonical">` tag disappears from topic pages, an SEO regression.
validated_findings.root_cause: Adding an explicit `render :show` inside `perform_show_response` moves template/layout rendering earlier than the `canonical_url` assignment that used to run before the implicit render.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the implicit render for `show` (e.g. render explicitly only from `unsubscribe`, or move the `canonical_url` call before `perform_show_response`).
validated_findings.title: Explicit `render :show` makes canonical_url in #show a no-op
validated_findings.trigger: Any crawler or non-XHR HTML request to a topic page (`topics#show`), which calls `perform_show_response` and only afterwards executes `canonical_url UrlHelper.absolute_without_cdn(...)`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that `render :show` at R500 causes canonical_url to be ignored is incorrect. In `#show`, `perform_show_response` is called at L85 and `canonical_url` at L87 - both before the implicit render. The explicit `render :show` only affects `#unsubscribe` which doesn't call `canonical_url`. No regression in `#show`.

validated_findings.body: Regressions such as the nil TopicUser 500, wrong notification-level transitions, or a broken slug redirect ship undetected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Untested new endpoint; defects in it are invisible to CI.
validated_findings.impact: Regressions such as the nil TopicUser 500, wrong notification-level transitions, or a broken slug redirect ship undetected.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new public controller endpoint with branching state mutation was added without any accompanying request/controller spec.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add specs in spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb covering: unauthenticated access, watching→regular, regular→muted, missing topic_users row, and the slug-less URL 301 redirect.
validated_findings.title: No controller spec covers the new topics#unsubscribe action
validated_findings.trigger: Running the suite: `spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb` contains no reference to `unsubscribe`, so the toggle logic, the login requirement, the slug redirect and the missing-TopicUser path are never exercised.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap findings are stylistic/process observations, not concrete defects introduced by the patch. Absence of tests is not a bug in the code itself. The finding describes missing coverage rather than a proven defect with trigger and impact.

validated_findings.body: A misspelled public property is baked into the template contract (`{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`), making later lookups/refactors error-prone and cheap-to-fix only now.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability: misspelled identifier propagated across controller and template.
validated_findings.impact: A misspelled public property is baked into the template contract (`{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`), making later lookups/refactors error-prone and cheap-to-fix only now.
validated_findings.root_cause: Typo introduced in the new computed property identifier.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Rename to `stopNotificationsText` in the controller and update `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` accordingly.
validated_findings.title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
validated_findings.trigger: Any developer referencing the property from the template or another module; the identifier reads "Notificiations".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Typo 'stopNotificiationsText' is a stylistic/naming issue, not a functional bug. The code works correctly - the misspelled property is consistently used in both controller (R5) and template. This is explicitly excluded as a stylistic finding.

validated_findings.body: The notification reason paragraph rendered by `topic-notifications-button` (longDescription alias) is not suppressed, or reappears after the first level change, contradicting the stated intent of the code.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Intended UI suppression silently does not take effect.
validated_findings.impact: The notification reason paragraph rendered by `topic-notifications-button` (longDescription alias) is not suppressed, or reappears after the first level change, contradicting the stated intent of the code.
validated_findings.root_cause: The route mutates a computed property that has no setter, so the assignment is either clobbered or recomputed by its dependent keys.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Suppress the text at the render site instead, e.g. pass an explicit `longDescription=null` / add a `showDescription=false` flag to the component invocation in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs rather than setting a computed property.
validated_findings.title: afterModel sets a getter-only computed property, so the reason text is not hidden
validated_findings.trigger: Navigating to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe: `notificationReasonText` is defined in topic-details.js.es6 as `function() {...}.property('notification_level', 'notifications_reason_id')` with no setter, and its dependent key changes again as soon as the user picks a level in the notifications dropdown.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that setting `details.notificationReasonText` to null fails because it's a computed property without setter is speculative. Ember allows setting properties that shadow computed properties. No concrete evidence the assignment fails or that the text reappears. The patch code at R14 may work as intended.

validated_findings.body: I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument and the email fails to build/send.
validated_findings.evidence: To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).
validated_findings.failure_mode: Runtime I18n interpolation error for callers that do not supply the new option.
validated_findings.impact: I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument and the email fails to build/send.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new mandatory interpolation variable was added to a shared locale string without providing a default in the builder that renders it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Default `unsubscribe_url` in `MessageBuilder#initialize` template_args (e.g. to the user preferences URL) or only append the topic sentence when `@opts[:unsubscribe_url]` is present.
validated_findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires %{unsubscribe_url} with no fallback
validated_findings.trigger: Any caller of `build_email` that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without an `unsubscribe_url` option (plugins, future mailers); `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` then call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows `unsubscribe_url` is passed by `user_notifications.rb` at line 295 when calling `build_email`. The spec at R172 also passes it. The claim assumes callers don't provide the variable, but the patch itself shows the primary caller does provide it. No proven failure path.

validated_findings.body: The confirmation page tells the user they will stop receiving notifications while they will keep receiving reply/mention notifications for that topic, generating confusion and repeat unsubscribes.
validated_findings.evidence: stop_notifications: "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."
validated_findings.failure_mode: Documentation/UI text does not match implemented behavior.
validated_findings.impact: The confirmation page tells the user they will stop receiving notifications while they will keep receiving reply/mention notifications for that topic, generating confusion and repeat unsubscribes.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new user-facing string describes a full mute while the server-side toggle only steps the level down by one for watching/tracking topics.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Word the string to match the actual transition (e.g. "You will no longer be notified of every new post in {{title}}") or return the resulting level and pick the message accordingly.
validated_findings.title: Unsubscribe copy overstates the effect for watching/tracking topics
validated_findings.trigger: A user at notification level watching or tracking clicks the email unsubscribe link; the controller only downgrades the level to `regular` (TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]), which still notifies on replies to their posts and mentions.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a documentation/UX accuracy concern, not a code defect. The locale string at R985 describes stopping notifications, while code sets level to regular (still gets some notifications). This is a design/copy decision, not a bug with concrete runtime impact.

validated_findings.body: The new per-topic unsubscribe link can silently vanish from notification email bodies without any spec failing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Test exercises the new input path without verifying its output, giving false coverage confidence.
validated_findings.impact: The new per-topic unsubscribe link can silently vanish from notification email bodies without any spec failing.
validated_findings.root_cause: The spec was extended with the new option but no assertion was added for the behavior that option enables.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add an expectation such as `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to match("/t/1234/unsubscribe")` alongside the existing user-preferences-url assertion.
validated_findings.title: Message builder spec adds unsubscribe_url but asserts nothing about it
validated_findings.trigger: Running the suite after removing `%{unsubscribe_url}` from the `unsubscribe_link` locale or dropping the option from `user_notifications.rb`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap findings are process observations. The spec adds `unsubscribe_url` option at R172 but doesn't assert on it. While this could be improved, missing assertions are not code defects - they're test quality issues explicitly excluded from valid findings.
